tasks.title: Sec A · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What did the man want to discuss with the woman?

options.A: Changing his major.
options.B: His family situation.
options.C: Revising his graduation thesis.
options.D: His passion for Art History.

questions.cn: 男士想和女士商量什么？

optionsCn.A: 换专业。
optionsCn.C: 修改毕业论文。
optionsCn.D: 他对艺术史的热情。

questions.stem: Why does the man want to give up Art History?

options.A: He doesn’t think it legitimate to depend on his father.
options.B: He thinks his financial situation has now changed.
options.C: He doesn’t think it will provide him with a living.
options.D: He thinks it nourishes the financially secure only.

questions.cn: 男士为什么想放弃艺术史？

optionsCn.A: 他觉得依赖父亲不正当。
optionsCn.B: 他认为自己的财务状况已经改变。
optionsCn.C: 他认为这一专业无法让他谋生。
optionsCn.D: 他认为它只滋养经济上有保障的人。

questions.stem: What does the woman advise the man to do?

options.A: Try his best to socialize and build a network in the art industry.
options.B: Seek financially viable employment opportunities after graduation.
options.C: Investigate all possible ways to become a celebrity in the art world.
options.D: Strike a balance between intellectual pursuits and financial security.

questions.cn: 女士建议男士怎么做？

optionsCn.A: 尽力去社交、在艺术行业建立人脉。
optionsCn.B: 毕业后寻找经济上可行的就业机会。
optionsCn.C: 研究一切在艺术界成名的可能途径。
optionsCn.D: 在精神追求与经济保障之间取得平衡。

questions.stem: What does the man say he really lacks right now?

options.A: Money.
options.B: Time.
options.C: Determination.
options.D: Optimism.

questions.cn: 男士说他现在真正缺少什么？

optionsCn.A: 钱。
optionsCn.C: 决心。
optionsCn.D: 乐观。

lines.t: Hi, Alan.
lines.cn: 嗨，艾伦。

lines.t: Sorry for not calling you back sooner.
lines.cn: 抱歉没有早点回你电话。

lines.t: You said on the phone you had something you needed to discuss with me?
lines.cn: 你在电话里说有事要和我商量？

lines.t: Well, to get right down to it, I’m having second thoughts about my major.
lines.cn: 嗯，直说吧，我对自己的专业动摇了。

lines.t: With my family situation getting more complicated and the end of my university education nearing, persisting with Art History just doesn’t seem the right choice.
lines.cn: 家里情况越来越复杂，大学教育又快到头了，继续读艺术史似乎不是对的选择。

lines.t: Alan, in the last three years, I have heard nothing but how passionate you are about the Art History programme.
lines.cn: 艾伦，这三年里我听到的全是你多么热爱艺术史这个专业。

lines.t: You often told fellow classmates how fabulous the instructors were and that you finally felt accepted.
lines.cn: 你常跟同学说老师们有多棒，说你终于感到被接纳了。

lines.t: What would cause you to abandon it?
lines.cn: 什么会让你放弃它呢？

lines.t: My father’s current financial situation has helped me realize that a more financially viable employment opportunity is not necessarily a bad thing.
lines.cn: 我父亲目前的财务状况让我意识到，一份经济上更可行的就业机会未必是坏事。

lines.t: Art History nourishes my soul, but does nothing to put food on my plate.
lines.cn: 艺术史滋养我的灵魂，却不能给我换来饭吃。

lines.t: What about all the work opportunities I discussed with you last month?
lines.cn: 那我上个月跟你聊过的那些工作机会呢？

lines.t: Have you gone to those places of business to investigate whether any legitimate positions might be available for someone with your background?
lines.cn: 你有没有去那些公司打听过，看看有没有适合你背景的正经职位？

lines.t: Um, well...
lines.cn: 呃，这个……

lines.t: Look, Alan, if your heart is set on working in the art industry, you need to be more assertive and start talking with people.
lines.cn: 听着，艾伦，如果你一心要进艺术行业，你就得更主动一些，开始和人打交道。

lines.t: Networking is key if you want to become a celebrity in the world of museums and galleries.
lines.cn: 如果你想在博物馆和画廊圈里成名，人脉是关键。

lines.t: Time is a very precious commodity right now.
lines.cn: 现在时间是非常宝贵的资源。

lines.t: My social life does not exist.
lines.cn: 我根本没有社交生活。

lines.t: I can barely keep up with my studies and thesis is due by the end of this year.
lines.cn: 我连学业都快跟不上了，论文年底就要交。

lines.t: When can I find time to research jobs when I have so much to do as it is?
lines.cn: 手头事情已经这么多，我上哪儿找时间去找工作？

lines.t: What you do now will determine your future options.
lines.cn: 你现在所做的，会决定你未来的选择。

lines.t: Now is the optimum time to put forth your best effort.
lines.cn: 现在正是全力以赴的最佳时机。

lines.t: I will take what you said into consideration.
lines.cn: 我会把你说的考虑进去。

lines.t: The advice is much appreciated.
lines.cn: 非常感谢你的建议。

tasks.title: Sec A · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What are the speakers mainly talking about in the conversation?

options.A: Their decision on investigating beef consumption.
options.B: Their original ideas about the domestic market.
options.C: Their different approaches to a case study.
options.D: Their end-of-semester business projects.

questions.cn: 两位说话人在对话中主要在谈什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们关于调查牛肉消费的决定。
optionsCn.B: 他们对国内市场的最初想法。
optionsCn.C: 他们对案例研究的不同做法。
optionsCn.D: 他们的期末商务项目。

questions.stem: What does the man say makes perfect sense?

options.A: Expanding farmland out west.
options.B: Importing most of the beef.
options.C: Raising cattle domestically.
options.D: Continuing to boost economic growth.

questions.cn: 男士说什么完全说得通？

optionsCn.A: 在西部扩大农田。
optionsCn.C: 在国内养牛。
optionsCn.D: 继续推动经济增长。

questions.stem: What business does the woman say has a vast and continual market?

options.A: Technical equipment.
options.B: Business consultancy.
options.C: Beef.
options.D: Carwashing.

questions.cn: 女士说哪门生意有巨大而持续的市场？

optionsCn.A: 技术设备。
optionsCn.C: 牛肉。
optionsCn.D: 洗车。

questions.stem: Who would the man’s imagined business cater to?

options.A: Car owners of all walks of life.
options.B: High-end customers in big cities.
options.C: Consumers craving for professional service.
options.D: Well-off dealers seeking a profitable markup.

questions.cn: 男士设想的生意会面向谁？

optionsCn.A: 各行各业的车主。
optionsCn.C: 渴望专业服务的消费者。
optionsCn.D: 寻求可观溢价收入的富裕经销商。

lines.t: Have you decided yet what your end-of-semester business project will be on?
lines.cn: 你想好这学期末的商务项目做什么了吗？

lines.t: Yes.
lines.cn: 想好了。

lines.t: How about you?
lines.cn: 你呢？

lines.t: Yes.
lines.cn: 想好了。

lines.t: Go on.
lines.cn: 说吧。

lines.t: You go first.
lines.cn: 你先说。

lines.t: I’m going to do it about beef.
lines.cn: 我打算做牛肉。

lines.t: Beef?
lines.cn: 牛肉？

lines.t: Yeah, beef.
lines.cn: 对，牛肉。

lines.t: I’m going to design a business case study for a cow farm that supplies beef for the domestic market.
lines.cn: 我要为一家供应国内市场的肉牛场设计一份商业案例研究。

lines.t: Well, that sounds very interesting and original.
lines.cn: 嗯，这听起来很有意思，也很有原创性。

lines.t: Where ever did you get that idea?
lines.cn: 你这主意到底是从哪儿来的？

lines.t: I don’t know. It just came to me, I guess. But think about it.
lines.cn: 不知道。我想就是灵光一闪吧。但你想想看。

lines.t: Beef consumption has been rising strongly over the past 20 years.
lines.cn: 过去 20 年牛肉消费一直在强劲增长。

lines.t: As the economy continues to grow, consumer demand is expected to continue to increase for the foreseeable future.
lines.cn: 随着经济持续增长，消费者需求在可预见的未来预计还会继续上升。

lines.t: And currently, most of the beef is imported, which brings with it added fees.
lines.cn: 而且目前大部分牛肉靠进口，这就带来了额外费用。

lines.t: So why not raise cattle here?
lines.cn: 那为什么不在本地养牛呢？

lines.t: Of course. Makes perfect sense.
lines.cn: 当然。完全说得通。

lines.t: There’s plenty of land out west.
lines.cn: 西部有大片土地。

lines.t: So, if done right, it should be very profitable to raise our own cattle.
lines.cn: 所以，如果做得好，自己养牛应该很赚钱。

lines.t: Exactly.
lines.cn: 正是。

lines.t: Seriously, that sounds like a great idea.
lines.cn: 说真的，这想法很棒。

lines.t: You should genuinely look into it once we get our degrees.
lines.cn: 等我们拿到学位，你真该认真研究一下。

lines.t: Thanks.
lines.cn: 谢谢。

lines.t: So, your turn now.
lines.cn: 那轮到你了。

lines.t: What are you doing your case study on?
lines.cn: 你的案例研究做什么？

lines.t: I was thinking about a car wash, but it now seems like such a boring notion after hearing your brilliant idea.
lines.cn: 我本来想做洗车行，但听完你这个绝妙的主意，它现在显得好无聊。

lines.t: That’s cool.
lines.cn: 挺好啊。

lines.t: I could see that working.
lines.cn: 我看得出来这事能成。

lines.t: After all, there’s plenty of cars about and those aren’t going away anytime soon.
lines.cn: 毕竟到处都有的是车，而且短期内车不会消失。

lines.t: While many people don’t care how their car looks, many other people do.
lines.cn: 虽然很多人不在乎自己的车看起来怎么样，但也有很多人很在乎。

lines.t: You got yourself a vast and continual market.
lines.cn: 你手上是一个巨大而持续的市场。

lines.t: Right.
lines.cn: 对。

lines.t: So the idea is a large self-cleaning car wash, but I mean really big and well-outfitted like they have in America.
lines.cn: 所以这个想法是建一家大型自助洗车场，我说的是像美国那种真正大型、设备齐全的。

lines.t: I was thinking of having it cater to high-end consumers in large cities.
lines.cn: 我打算让它面向大城市的高端消费者。

lines.t: It could charge a profitable markup by offering just a bit more technical equipment and professional service than competitors.
lines.cn: 只要比竞争对手多一点点技术设备和专业服务，就能收取可观的溢价。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 3 组
tasks.context: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do we learn from a new study about young children?

options.A: Parents’ talking with them during TV time raises their curiosity levels.
options.B: Their daily television exposure cuts parent-child conversation time.
options.C: The more TV they watch the poorer their progress in development.
options.D: Their socioeconomic levels impact their academic achievement.

questions.cn: 关于幼儿，我们从这项新研究中了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 父母在电视时间与他们交谈会提高他们的好奇心水平。
optionsCn.B: 他们每天看电视挤占了亲子交谈时间。
optionsCn.C: 他们看电视越多，发展进步越差。
optionsCn.D: 他们的社会经济水平影响学业成绩。

questions.stem: What did Prachi Shah’s study specifically focus on?

options.A: Kids’ enhanced learning.
options.B: Kids’ curiosity levels.
options.C: Kids’ reading and math.
options.D: Kids’ behavioral development.

questions.cn: 普拉奇·沙阿的研究特别关注什么？

optionsCn.A: 孩子学习能力的提升。
optionsCn.C: 孩子的阅读和数学。
optionsCn.D: 孩子的行为发展。

questions.stem: What does the passage say about excessive media exposure?

options.A: It can hinder kids from getting on with their peers.
options.B: It can cut into kids’ time on exploratory activities.
options.C: It can arouse kids’ interest in how people interact in real life.
options.D: It can widen the gap between kids from different economic statuses.

questions.cn: 关于过度媒体暴露，文章说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它会妨碍孩子与同龄人相处。
optionsCn.B: 它会挤占孩子做探索性活动的时间。
optionsCn.C: 它会激起孩子对现实中人际互动的兴趣。
optionsCn.D: 它会拉大不同经济状况孩子之间的差距。

lines.t: Increased television time for young children has long been linked with poorer progress in some areas of development.
lines.cn: 幼儿看电视时间增加，长期以来一直与某些发展领域进步较差相关联。

lines.t: One possible way to counter those negative effects is talking while watching the screen.
lines.cn: 抵消这些负面影响的一个可行办法，是看电视时同时交谈。

lines.t: As a new study suggests, the more parents engaged in conversation with preschoolers during TV time, the more likely those children were to have higher curiosity levels when they reached kindergarten.
lines.cn: 一项新研究显示，父母在电视时间与学龄前孩子交谈越多，这些孩子到了幼儿园阶段好奇心水平越可能更高。

lines.t: This was particularly true for children with socioeconomic disadvantages.
lines.cn: 在社会经济条件不利的孩子身上，这一点尤其明显。

lines.t: “Our findings reinforce the importance of parent conversation to promote early childhood development and curiosity,” said lead author Prachi Shah at University of Michigan Health C. S. Mott Children’s Hospital.
lines.cn: 密歇根大学健康中心 C. S. 莫特儿童医院的论文第一作者普拉奇·沙阿说：“我们的发现强化了父母交谈对促进幼儿发展和好奇心的重要性。”

lines.t: Researchers assessed hours of daily television exposure and frequency of parent screen-time conversation among 1,500 preschoolers, and then measured early childhood curiosity in kindergarten.
lines.cn: 研究者评估了 1500 名学龄前儿童每天看电视的小时数以及父母在屏幕时间交谈的频率，随后测量了他们上幼儿园时的幼儿期好奇心。

lines.t: The study specifically focused on curiosity levels, which are associated with enhanced learning and higher academic achievement in reading and math at kindergarten, and behavioral-developmental benefits, especially for children from families with lower socioeconomic status.
lines.cn: 该研究特别关注好奇心水平，因为好奇心与幼儿园阶段更好的学习和更高的阅读、数学学业成绩相关，也带来行为发展方面的益处，对来自社会经济地位较低家庭的孩子尤其如此。

lines.t: While many young children are now growing up with digital media exposure through mobile devices like tablets and phones, television remains a dominant screen activity, accounting for 72% of all screen time.
lines.cn: 尽管如今许多幼儿是伴随着平板、手机等移动设备的数字媒体暴露长大的，电视仍是占主导地位的屏幕活动，占全部屏幕时间的 72%。

lines.t: TVs are in 98% of all homes, keeping television exposure a relevant developmental context in young children.
lines.cn: 98% 的家庭都有电视，因此电视暴露仍是幼儿发展中一个重要的环境因素。

lines.t: Excessive media exposure, including television, can displace exploratory activities such as play and parent-child interactions, which are believed to be key to cultivating curiosity in kids.
lines.cn: 包括电视在内的过度媒体暴露，会挤占玩耍、亲子互动等探索性活动，而这些活动被认为对培养孩子的好奇心至关重要。

lines.t: “Our findings suggest the importance of parents finding opportunities to foster conversational exchanges in daily routines with their young children-including while watching television,” Shah said.
lines.cn: 沙阿说：“我们的发现表明，父母在日常生活中有必要寻找机会与幼儿进行对话交流——包括在看电视的时候。”

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 4 组
tasks.context: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What is the dark side of our inborn drive to acquire?

options.A: Exerting ourselves too hard in order to attain our life’s goals.
options.B: Being possessed with a single thought of professional success.
options.C: Trying every means to beat others in terms of personal aspirations.
options.D: Being mindlessly driven to possess more and more material things.

questions.cn: 我们天生获取欲的阴暗面是什么？

optionsCn.A: 为了人生目标而过度透支自己。
optionsCn.B: 满脑子只想着职业成功。
optionsCn.C: 为个人志向不择手段胜过他人。
optionsCn.D: 不知不觉地被驱使着占有越来越多的物质。

questions.stem: What might happen if we do not harness our inborn drive to acquire?

options.A: We might isolate ourselves from our fellow beings.
options.B: We might acquire an incorrect sense of well-being.
options.C: We might end up pursuing all the wrong things.
options.D: We might make a mess of our personal lives.

questions.cn: 如果我们不驾驭天生的获取欲，可能会怎样？

optionsCn.A: 我们可能把自己与同类隔离开来。
optionsCn.B: 我们可能形成错误的幸福感。
optionsCn.C: 我们最终可能追求所有错误的东西。
optionsCn.D: 我们可能把自己的个人生活搞得一团糟。

questions.stem: What does the passage say about our intentional aspirational goals?

options.A: They should be based on solid theoretical concepts.
options.B: They should take personal interests into account.
options.C: They should include goals to help other people.
options.D: They should increase our sense of worthiness.

questions.cn: 关于我们自觉的志向目标，文章说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它们应建立在扎实的理论概念之上。
optionsCn.B: 它们应把个人兴趣考虑在内。
optionsCn.C: 它们应包括帮助他人的目标。
optionsCn.D: 它们应提升我们的自我价值感。

questions.stem: What will you end up doing without pursuing intentional aspirational goals?

options.A: Drifting through life aimlessly.
options.B: Giving up the chance to fulfill yourself.
options.C: Abandoning all that life has to offer.
options.D: Spoiling your character and integrity.

questions.cn: 不追求自觉的志向目标，你最终会怎样？

optionsCn.A: 漫无目的地随波逐流度过一生。
optionsCn.C: 抛弃生活所提供的一切。
optionsCn.D: 败坏自己的品格与正直。

lines.t: Humans are aspirational goal seeking beings.
lines.cn: 人类是不断追求目标、渴望进取的生物。

lines.t: Each of us, according to research, has an inborn drive to acquire.
lines.cn: 研究显示，我们每个人天生都有获取的驱动力。

lines.t: The “dark side” of this drive to acquire is being mindlessly driven to possess more and more “things” and to socially compare our “stuff” with all the stuff other people have in their lives.
lines.cn: 这种获取欲的“阴暗面”，是不知不觉地被驱使着占有越来越多的“东西”，并在社交上把自己拥有的“东西”与别人生活里的东西相比较。

lines.t: So the question is, how do we ensure we tap into our drive to acquire in positive ways that will benefit our well-being?
lines.cn: 所以问题在于：我们如何确保以有益于自身福祉的积极方式去利用这种获取欲？

lines.t: One way is to become more intentionally aspirational.
lines.cn: 一种办法是变得更有意识地“志向化”。

lines.t: To be intentionally aspirational includes consciously aspiring to be the person you need to be to succeed in your professional and personal life.
lines.cn: 有意识地志向化，包括自觉地立志成为那个要在职业和个人生活中获得成功所需要的自己。

lines.t: It also includes consciously aspiring to acquire things in your life that will positively impact your sense of well-being.
lines.cn: 它还包括自觉地立志获取那些会对你的幸福感产生积极影响的东西。

lines.t: If you’re not consciously, mindfully, and intentionally harnessing this inborn drive to acquire, you might be mindlessly pursuing all the wrong things.
lines.cn: 如果你没有自觉、有心、有意地驾驭这种天生的获取欲，你就可能在不知不觉地追求所有错误的东西。

lines.t: While your intentional aspirational goals will include the pursuit of acquiring things that will increase your sense of well-being, they ought to also include goals to help other people in your various life roles.
lines.cn: 你自觉的志向目标会包括追求能提升幸福感的东西，同时也应当包括在你的各种人生角色中帮助他人的目标。

lines.t: Your intentional aspirational goals will also include striving to be your personal best-a person of “good” character, integrity, and trustworthiness.
lines.cn: 你自觉的志向目标还会包括努力成为最好的自己——一个品格“优良”、正直、值得信赖的人。

lines.t: Think about this from a practical, rather than theoretical viewpoint.
lines.cn: 从实际而非理论的角度来想想这一点。

lines.t: If you’re not pursuing intentional aspirational goals, you have nothing to strive for.
lines.cn: 如果你不追求自觉的志向目标，你就没有什么可为之努力。

lines.t: If you have nothing to strive for, you’re putting yourself in the dangerous position of simply drifting through life, and you will not be able to experience, live and enjoy all that life has to offer.
lines.cn: 如果你没有什么可为之努力，你就把自己置于随波逐流度过一生的危险境地，也无法体验、活出并享受生活所提供的一切。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 5 组
tasks.context: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the speaker recommend in this talk?

options.A: Grade-raising ways and means.
options.B: Pressure-alleviating exercise.
options.C: Revision-conducting approaches.
options.D: Brain-boosting food and drink.

questions.cn: 讲话者在这段讲话中推荐什么？

optionsCn.A: 提高成绩的途径和办法。
optionsCn.C: 进行复习的方法。
optionsCn.D: 健脑的食物和饮品。

questions.stem: What does the speaker warn against about coffee?

options.A: Buying it from coffee shops.
options.B: Building up a tolerance of it.
options.C: Drinking it after 2 pm.
options.D: Consuming it with sugar.

questions.cn: 关于咖啡，讲话者提出了什么警告？

optionsCn.A: 从咖啡店买咖啡。
optionsCn.C: 下午两点后喝咖啡。
optionsCn.D: 加糖喝咖啡。

questions.stem: How can we get sufficient nutrients according to the speaker?

options.A: By taking varied vitamin supplements.
options.B: By consuming a rich variety of foods.
options.C: By eating both oranges and frozen berries.
options.D: By getting components packaged in tablets.

questions.cn: 根据讲话者，我们如何获得充足的营养？

optionsCn.A: 服用各种维生素补充剂。
optionsCn.C: 既吃橙子又吃冷冻浆果。
optionsCn.D: 获取打包在药片里的成分。

lines.t: It’s revision time for exams and dissertations.
lines.cn: 又到了为考试和论文复习的时候。

lines.t: The pressure is on, so you want all the help you can get to aid your memory and raise your grades.
lines.cn: 压力来了，所以你想尽可能多寻求帮助来增强记忆、提高成绩。

lines.t: As a nutrition expert, I want to say that eating well can make a real difference to your revision regime.
lines.cn: 作为一名营养专家，我想说，吃得好能实实在在改善你的复习状态。

lines.t: So what brain-boosting food and drink would I recommend?
lines.cn: 那么，我会推荐哪些健脑的食物和饮品？

lines.t: Coffee can have numerous benefits.
lines.cn: 咖啡可以有很多好处。

lines.t: However, while coffee may make you more alert, individuals can build up a tolerance, meaning this is short-lived.
lines.cn: 然而，咖啡虽然能让你更清醒，但个人会产生耐受性，这意味着这种效果很短暂。

lines.t: Coffee can also increase blood sugar and eventually cause lack of focus and energy.
lines.cn: 咖啡还会升高血糖，最终导致注意力和精力不足。

lines.t: It’s also worth noting that people react differently to coffee.
lines.cn: 同样值得注意的是，人们对咖啡的反应各不相同。

lines.t: Some people can drink it at midnight and go straight to sleep, whereas others get feelings of anxiety after a small amount.
lines.cn: 有人半夜喝了也能马上睡着，而有人喝一点点就感到焦虑。

lines.t: Also remember that coffee from a coffee shop may be stronger than coffee made at home, so stop drinking coffee by 2 pm and have a maximum of two cups of coffee a day, but be aware of your own reaction to it.
lines.cn: 还要记住，咖啡店的咖啡可能比家里做的更浓，所以下午两点后不要再喝咖啡，每天最多两杯，但要留意你自己的反应。

lines.t: Whole grain foods will ward off hunger.
lines.cn: 全谷物食物能抵御饥饿。

lines.t: Examples include porridge and whole wheat bread.
lines.cn: 比如燕麦粥和全麦面包。

lines.t: Combining whole grain foods with protein will help keep your blood sugar levels balanced, which is essential for mood and concentration.
lines.cn: 把全谷物食物与蛋白质搭配，有助于保持血糖水平平稳，这对情绪和注意力至关重要。

lines.t: Berries and nuts are a convenient and nutritious snack.
lines.cn: 浆果和坚果是方便又有营养的零食。

lines.t: Blueberries, like many dark colored fruits and vegetables, can slow down brain damage and age-related decline.
lines.cn: 蓝莓和许多深色果蔬一样，能减缓脑损伤和与年龄相关的衰退。

lines.t: Frozen berries are also a good choice.
lines.cn: 冷冻浆果也是不错的选择。

lines.t: They are usually cheap, last longer, and don’t lose their nutrients when frozen.
lines.cn: 它们通常便宜、保存更久，冷冻时也不会损失营养。

lines.t: But flavored and coated nuts are less healthy, as they contain added oil, salt, and sugar.
lines.cn: 但调味和裹衣坚果就没那么健康，因为其中添加了油、盐和糖。

lines.t: Doctors often recommend taking vitamin supplements to top up on the nutrients you need.
lines.cn: 医生常建议服用维生素补充剂来补足所需营养。

lines.t: But I would say food should always come before supplements and the key to getting as many nutrients as possible is to eat a varied diet, with lots of different colors such as frozen berries and dark green vegetables.
lines.cn: 但我要说，食物永远应当优先于补充剂；尽可能摄入多种营养的关键是饮食多样，包含各种不同颜色的食物，比如冷冻浆果和深绿色蔬菜。

lines.t: It’s better to get everything you need from food and drink.
lines.cn: 最好从食物和饮品中获取你所需的一切。

lines.t: For example, oranges contain not only vitamin C, which boosts the immune system, but also fiber and other components that you can’t get packaged together in a tablet.
lines.cn: 例如，橙子不仅含有增强免疫力的维生素 C，还含有纤维和其他成分，这些是无法一起打包进一片药片里的。

lines.t: Don’t forget to drink a proper amount of water, which can boost attention by almost 25%, and can elevate your mood as well.
lines.cn: 别忘了喝足量的水，它能把注意力提高近 25%，也能改善情绪。

lines.t: Finally, don’t skip meals.
lines.cn: 最后，不要不吃饭。

lines.t: Eating regularly will help keep blood sugar balanced and feed the brain with the fuel it needs.
lines.cn: 规律进食有助于保持血糖平衡，并为大脑提供所需的燃料。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 6 组
tasks.context: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What is the worrying trend the late Swedish academic has identified?

options.A: Many people across advanced economies think the world is going from bad to worse.
options.B: The news focuses on reporting catastrophes that occur across the world.
options.C: A significant part of the world is experiencing another great recession.
options.D: Many people have no idea of those living under miserable conditions.

questions.cn: 这位已故瑞典学者指出的令人担忧的趋势是什么？

optionsCn.A: 发达经济体的许多人认为世界正在变得越来越糟。
optionsCn.B: 新闻专注于报道世界各地发生的灾难。
optionsCn.C: 世界上相当一部分地区正经历又一次大衰退。
optionsCn.D: 许多人对生活在悲惨条件下的人一无所知。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about globalization?

options.A: It has experienced ups and downs like any other historical trend.
options.B: It is hailed as a miracle by both economists and ordinary people.
options.C: It is the only way for all countries to share economic prosperity.
options.D: It has given more and more countries a rare chance to thrive.

questions.cn: 关于全球化，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它像其他历史趋势一样有起有落。
optionsCn.B: 它被经济学家和普通人共同誉为奇迹。
optionsCn.C: 它是所有国家共享经济繁荣的唯一途径。
optionsCn.D: 它给越来越多国家提供了难得的繁荣机会。

questions.stem: What do we learn about half of the global population?

options.A: Their fortunes may take a downturn.
options.B: They can be classified as middle class.
options.C: Their living standards have been deteriorating.
options.D: They are experiencing a radical transformation.

questions.cn: 关于全球一半人口，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们的好日子可能变差。
optionsCn.B: 他们可以被归为中产阶级。
optionsCn.C: 他们的生活水平一直在恶化。
optionsCn.D: 他们正经历一场彻底的转变。

lines.t: The late Swedish academic Hans Rosling has identified a worrying trend:
lines.cn: 已故的瑞典学者汉斯·罗斯林指出了一个令人担忧的趋势：

lines.t: not only do many people across advanced economies have no idea that the world is becoming a much better place,
lines.cn: 不仅发达经济体的许多人根本不知道世界正在变得好得多，

lines.t: but they actually even think the opposite.
lines.cn: 他们甚至认为情况正好相反。

lines.t: This is no wonder, when the news focuses on reporting catastrophes, terrorist attacks, wars and famines.
lines.cn: 这也难怪，因为新闻总在报道灾难、恐怖袭击、战争和饥荒。

lines.t: Who wants to hear about the fact that every day, some 200,000 people around the world are lifted above the $2-a-day poverty line?
lines.cn: 谁想听这样的消息：每天全世界约有 20 万人摆脱了每日 2 美元的贫困线？

lines.t: Or that more than 300,000 people get access to electricity and clean water for the first time every day?
lines.cn: 或者每天有 30 多万人第一次用上电和干净的水？

lines.t: These stories of people in low-income countries simply don’t make for exciting news coverage.
lines.cn: 这些低收入国家人们的故事，根本算不上吸引眼球的新闻。

lines.t: But, as Rosling pointed out in his book Factfulness, it’s important to put all the bad news in perspective.
lines.cn: 但正如罗斯林在《事实》一书中所指出的，重要的是把所有坏消息放在整体中看。

lines.t: While it is true that globalization has put some downward pressure on middle-class wages in advanced economies in recent decades,
lines.cn: 近几十年来，全球化确实对发达经济体的中产阶级工资造成了一定下行压力，

lines.t: it has also helped lift hundreds of millions of people above the global poverty line.
lines.cn: 但它也帮助数亿人摆脱了全球贫困线。

lines.t: If we really care about global welfare, globalization is the only way forward to ensure that economic prosperity is shared among all countries and not only a select few advanced economies.
lines.cn: 如果我们真的关心全球福祉，全球化就是唯一的前进道路，能确保经济繁荣为所有国家共享，而不只是少数几个发达经济体。

lines.t: While some people glorify the past,
lines.cn: 有些人美化过去，

lines.t: one of the big facts of economic history is that until quite recently a significant part of the world population has lived under quite miserable conditions-and this has been true throughout most of human history.
lines.cn: 但经济史上的一大事实是：直到不久之前，世界人口中相当一部分一直生活在相当悲惨的条件下——这在人类历史的大部分时间里都是如此。

lines.t: While there were many long-lasting ups and downs, like the Great Depression or the recent Great Recession,
lines.cn: 虽然其间有许多持久的起落，比如大萧条或近期的大衰退，

lines.t: the constancy of the long-run growth rate is actually quite miraculous.
lines.cn: 但长期增长率的稳定实际上堪称奇迹。

lines.t: Low-income countries, including China and India, have been growing at a significantly faster pace in recent decades and are quickly catching up to the West.
lines.cn: 包括中国和印度在内的低收入国家，近几十年来增速显著更快，正迅速追赶西方。

lines.t: A 10% growth rate over a prolonged period means that income levels double roughly every seven years.
lines.cn: 长期保持 10% 的增长率意味着收入水平大约每七年翻一番。

lines.t: It is obviously good news if prosperity is more shared across the globe.
lines.cn: 繁荣在全球范围内更广泛地共享，显然是好事。

lines.t: While inequality within countries has gone up as a result of globalization,
lines.cn: 虽然全球化导致各国内部的不平等上升，

lines.t: global inequality has been on a steady downward trend for several decades.
lines.cn: 但全球不平等几十年来一直呈稳步下降趋势。

lines.t: This is mostly a result of the improvement of hundreds of millions of people’s living standards.
lines.cn: 这主要是数亿人生活水平改善的结果。

lines.t: In fact, for the first time ever since the Industrial Revolution, about half of the global population can be considered middle class.
lines.cn: 事实上，自工业革命以来第一次，全球约一半人口可以算作中产阶级。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 7 组
tasks.context: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What question does the speaker try to answer in this talk?

options.A: Why smells can activate emotional memories.
options.B: How powerful the sense of smell can become.
options.C: How scent particles revive memories forgotten.
options.D: Why the scent of bread has a strong mental impact.

questions.cn: 讲话者在这次讲话中试图回答什么问题？

optionsCn.A: 气味为何能激活情感记忆。
optionsCn.C: 气味粒子如何唤回被遗忘的记忆。
optionsCn.D: 面包的气味为何有强烈的心理影响。

questions.stem: What is said to result in an intimate connection between emotions, memories and scents?

options.A: The brain cells’ processing of memories experienced as strongly emotional.
options.B: The activation of the brain’s emotion processing area by chemical particles.
options.C: The interaction between chemical particles and the brain cells responsible for smell.
options.D: The sensations of scents going directly to the brain’s emotional and memory centers.

questions.cn: 据说是什么造成了情绪、记忆与气味之间的紧密联系？

optionsCn.A: 脑细胞对强烈情感记忆的加工。
optionsCn.B: 化学粒子对大脑情绪加工区的激活。
optionsCn.C: 化学粒子与负责嗅觉的脑细胞之间的相互作用。
optionsCn.D: 气味的感觉直接传向大脑的情绪与记忆中枢。

questions.stem: What does the brain use to give meaning to information and find a memory?

options.A: Imagination.
options.B: Association.
options.C: Experience.
options.D: Context.

questions.cn: 大脑用什么来赋予信息意义、并找到一段记忆？

optionsCn.A: 想象。
optionsCn.C: 经验。
optionsCn.D: 情境。

questions.stem: What drawback do memories of scents share with other memories?

options.A: Inaccuracy and alterability.
options.B: Susceptibility to polar interpretations.
options.C: Being personal and individualistic.
options.D: Being dependent on relevant scenarios.

questions.cn: 气味唤起的记忆与其他记忆共有哪种缺陷？

optionsCn.A: 不准确且会改变。
optionsCn.C: 具有个人性和个体性。
optionsCn.D: 依赖于相关场景。

lines.t: We all know that the sense of smell is powerful.
lines.cn: 我们都知道嗅觉很强大。

lines.t: The delicious scent of bread, for example, can act like a time machine.
lines.cn: 比如，面包的香气可以像一台时光机。

lines.t: One sniff can bring back a memory from many years ago.
lines.cn: 吸一口气，就能唤回多年前的一段记忆。

lines.t: Indeed, scent particles, in general, can revive memories that have been long forgotten.
lines.cn: 的确，气味粒子通常能唤醒早已遗忘的记忆。

lines.t: But why do smells sometimes trigger powerful memories, especially emotional ones?
lines.cn: 但为什么气味有时会触发强烈的记忆，尤其是情感记忆？

lines.t: The short answer is that the brain regions that handle smells, memories and emotions are linked.
lines.cn: 简短的回答是：处理气味、记忆和情绪的大脑区域是相互连接的。

lines.t: A scent is a chemical particle that floats in through the nose and into the region of the brain responsible for smell, where the sensation is first processed into a form that the brain can read.
lines.cn: 气味是一种化学粒子，随呼吸进入鼻腔，到达大脑中负责嗅觉的区域，在那里感觉首先被加工成大脑能读取的形式。

lines.t: Brain cells then carry that information to the area of the brain where emotions are processed, and then to an adjacent area of the brain where learning and memory formation take place.
lines.cn: 随后脑细胞把这些信息传送到处理情绪的大脑区域，再传到相邻的、负责学习与记忆形成的大脑区域。

lines.t: Scents are the only sensations that travel such a direct path to the emotional and memory centers of the brain.
lines.cn: 气味是唯一沿着如此直接的路径抵达大脑情绪与记忆中枢的感觉。

lines.t: That results in an intimate connection between emotions, memories and scents, which is why memories triggered by scents are experienced as more emotional than those triggered by sight or sound.
lines.cn: 于是情绪、记忆和气味之间形成了紧密的联系，这就是为什么由气味触发的记忆，比由视觉或声音触发的记忆更具情感色彩。

lines.t: Let’s take a closer look at how those memories are activated.
lines.cn: 让我们更仔细地看看这些记忆是如何被激活的。

lines.t: Usually, when a person smells something that’s connected to a meaningful event in their past, they’ll first have an emotional response to the sensation and then a memory might follow.
lines.cn: 通常，当一个人闻到与过去某件有意义的事相关的气味时，会先对这个感觉产生情绪反应，随后记忆才可能出现。

lines.t: But sometimes, the memory doesn’t come to the surface.
lines.cn: 但有时，记忆并不会浮出水面。

lines.t: The person might feel the emotion of something that happened in the past but won’t remember what they experienced.
lines.cn: 这个人可能感受到过去某事的情绪，却想不起自己经历过什么。

lines.t: What causes this baffling phenomenon?
lines.cn: 是什么造成了这种令人困惑的现象？

lines.t: The explanation is context.
lines.cn: 答案是情境。

lines.t: Imagine this scenario: a person is walking down the street smelling a scent that they first encountered decades ago, which activates an emotional response.
lines.cn: 想象这样一种情形：一个人走在街上，闻到一种几十年前初次遇到的气味，这激活了情绪反应。

lines.t: If the person had first come across that smell in a very different context, it will be much more difficult to recover the associated memory, because the brain uses the context to give meaning to the information and find that memory.
lines.cn: 如果这个人当初是在一个非常不同的情境中初次遇到那种气味，那么找回相关记忆就会困难得多，因为大脑用情境来赋予信息意义、并找到那段记忆。

lines.t: The special nature of memories brought back by scents notwithstanding, they have the same drawbacks as other memories.
lines.cn: 尽管由气味唤起的记忆有其特殊性，它们也有与其他记忆相同的缺陷。

lines.t: They aren’t always accurate, and they can change over time.
lines.cn: 它们并不总是准确的，而且会随时间改变。

lines.t: In fact, each time we remember something, that memory can become distorted.
lines.cn: 事实上，我们每回忆一次，那段记忆就可能被扭曲一次。

lines.t: But, because of the strong emotional associations these memories evoke, people who remember something due to a scent are often convinced that the memories are accurate, even when they aren’t.
lines.cn: 但由于这些记忆引发的强烈情感联想，因气味而想起某事的人往往确信这些记忆是准确的——即便它们并不准确。
